_comment: Single source of truth for the Open Play Brick rev A wiring. The emulator draws its diagram from this file and tools/gen_pins.mjs generates firmware/core/pins.h from it, so the picture, the simulation and the firmware cannot drift apart.

board.name: Open Play Brick
board.envelope_note: 2 x 4 studs, five plates tall (5 x 3.2 mm), plus 1.7 mm studs

NFC_BUSY.desc: PN5180 BUSY handshake, high while the reader works

I2C_SCL.desc: I2C clock, 2.2k pull-up (also keeps the GPIO9 boot strap high)

IMU_INT1.desc: Motion interrupt, wakes the MCU from deep sleep (RTC-capable pad)

PERIPH_EN_N.desc: Low = switched 3V3 rail on. 10k pull-up keeps it off in reset and deep sleep, and satisfies the GPIO2 boot strap

USB_DP.desc: USB D+ (built-in USB Serial/JTAG: flashing and console)

3V3_SW.desc: Switched 3.3 V (NFC reader, pixels, amp enable). Off in deep sleep

parts.name: ESP32-C3FH4
parts.why: RISC-V MCU with 4 MB flash in-package, BLE 5 and Wi-Fi radio, native USB. Same silicon as the common ESP32-C3 Super Mini dev board, so the breadboard build and the brick board run one firmware.

parts.name: PN5180
parts.why: Full-power NFC frontend with ISO 15693 support. Already shown to read these tags in the Ellerbach project.

parts.name: Loop antenna
parts.package: PCB or flex loop, about 28 x 12 mm
parts.why: One coil around the board edge. Reads a tag on the top or bottom face. It cannot tell where on the brick a tag sits.

parts.name: LIS2DH12
parts.why: 3-axis, a few microamps in wake-on-motion mode, interrupt output that wakes the MCU.

parts.name: TCS34725
parts.why: RGB + clear light-to-digital converter with an IR filter. Used in the Ellerbach build.

parts.name: MAX17048
parts.why: Reports cell voltage, state of charge and charge rate over I2C, so no ADC pin is spent on the battery.

parts.name: MAX98357A
parts.why: Digital audio in, speaker out, no master clock and no DAC needed.

parts.name: SK6805-EC15 x 9
parts.why: Addressable RGB LEDs on one data wire. Pixels 0 to 7 are the light array, pixel 8 sits beside the colour sensor and lights the surface it looks at.

parts.name: P-FET load switch
parts.why: Cuts power to the reader and pixels in deep sleep. Nine idle pixels alone draw several milliamps.

parts.name: 3.3 V LDO
parts.why: Low-dropout, low quiescent current regulator, 300 mA class (for example TLV75533).

parts.name: MCP73831
parts.why: Single-cell linear charger, programmed to about 50 mA for a small cell.

parts.name: Li-Po cell
parts.package: 401225 pouch, 4 x 12 x 25 mm, about 100 mAh
parts.why: Widely sold pouch size with built-in protection board.

parts.name: USB-C
parts.why: Charging, flashing and serial console over one port.
